cause: The alleged extra provider round after a confirmation-ready proposal does not reproduce at the stated one-step boundary.
impact: At max_steps=1 the confirmed proposal ends with proposal_ready, makes exactly one provider request, and records no max_steps_exceeded; the original incident diagnosis is false rather than repaired by this line.
lesson: A terminal-state incident must be reproduced at its exact budget boundary before any remedy is named.

cause: The claimed covariance-language boundary is already present in the baseline Main Agent protocol.
impact: The transmitted protocol requires reporting only a covariance-assumption inference difference and prohibits calling nonrobust significance false or caused by heteroskedasticity absent a separate diagnostic; this is a model-input boundary, not a guarantee that a probabilistic provider can never disobey instructions.
lesson: For generated statistical prose, distinguish a tested instruction boundary from an unprovable guarantee about all future provider output.

cause: The claimed receipt-to-branch path and candidate-run limit are already defined by the baseline protocol and registry.
impact: The new regression demonstrates the published route with 8 and 20 visible candidates: one receipt lookup capped at 16 plus one branch-coefficient lookup, two tool executions and three provider requests in both cases. The four-run bound belongs to the coefficient reader, not the candidate receipt reader.
lesson: Measure tool-call count across differing overview sizes; a maxItems assertion alone cannot establish bounded path length.

cause: The claimed under-specified depends_on shape is already published and corrected by the baseline planner.

cause: The required elevated sandbox self-test was rejected by the execution platform due to the agent usage limit before it could establish a non-nested Seatbelt environment.

evidence.ref: 2026-07-31 elevated sandbox-exec self-test request rejected before command execution

impact: No current-line full gate can be claimed from this process. No sandbox weakening, skip, xfail, or indirect execution workaround was attempted.
lesson: When the execution authority cannot leave the nested workspace sandbox, retain the full-gate boundary and obtain equivalent evidence only from an explicitly authorized external terminal.

cause: The elevated sandbox self-test was rejected inside the agent platform, so no non-nested Seatbelt environment was available to that session.

evidence.ref: host terminal outside any agent sandbox, 2026-07-31: `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)' /bin/echo` printed sandbox-selftest-ok, then `bash scripts/gate.sh --full` on the current working tree: backend 4253 passed / 8 skipped / 1 xfailed, golden+invariants 23 passed, frontend 171 files / 1513 tests, tsc clean, >>> GATE PASSED; zero sandbox_apply failures

impact: The line could not produce its own full-gate evidence; the gate was instead run by the user in a host terminal outside any agent sandbox.
lesson: macOS refuses nested sandbox_apply, so a product that shells out to sandbox-exec cannot be gated from inside an agent sandbox; run the gate on the host.

impact: Five are recorded as satisfied by baseline 6607c2d and one as a non-reproducing diagnosis; none is counted as a v1.8.4 deliverable. The only new behaviour is the bounded-step regression. Two incidents stay open: notebook_load_not_found and chain_agent_proposal_upstream_error.
lesson: Closing an incident by citing pre-existing evidence and closing it by verifying a pre-existing capability are different acts; only the second is honest, and it must name the commit and line that provide the capability.
